summary: This script checks whether at least one Docker container is currently running. If no containers are found, it prints a yellow informational message to standard error and returns a failure code; otherwise it returns success. The comment notes that using parameter expansion is more efficient than piping output through grep.

explanations.5: docker ps -q -n 1 lists running containers (quiet mode, max 1 result), and -z checks if that output is empty—meaning no containers are running.
explanations.6: >&2 redirects the echo output to standard error instead of standard output, and \033[0;33m...\033[0m are ANSI escape codes that make the word 'Info:' display in yellow on compatible terminals.
